successCriteria.description: The test suite asserts that an owner cancelling their own DRAFT request transitions status to CANCELLED with cancelledBy = actor.id and cancelledAt set, and performs NO balance read or write (findByKeyCalls and updateCalls on the balance fake remain empty).

The test suite asserts that an owner cancelling their own SUBMITTED request releases the full requestedDays by decrementing pendingDays (pendingDays -= requestedDays) and leaves usedDays untouched, with the balance row read via findByKey with forUpdate=true before the write.

The test suite asserts that a direct manager cancelling an APPROVED request for their direct report releases the full requestedDays by decrementing usedDays (usedDays -= requestedDays) and leaves pendingDays untouched, with the balance row read via findByKey with forUpdate=true before the write.

The test suite asserts the authorization guards: ForbiddenError when a non-owner attempts to cancel a DRAFT/SUBMITTED request, when the owner attempts to cancel their own APPROVED request, and when a non-direct manager attempts to cancel an APPROVED request; and that an ADMIN cancels an APPROVED request for anyone without the direct-manager check.
The test suite asserts the timing guard: ConflictError when startDate is today or in the past (startDate <= today), and that a future startDate proceeds.

The test suite asserts the side effects: exactly one audit record with action AuditAction.CANCEL (entityType 'leave_request', entityId = request id, actorId = actor.id) and exactly one synchronous cancellation notification to the affected employee (recipientId = request.employeeId).

The test suite asserts atomicity via containment: uow.callCount === 1 and every repository/service call (repository.update, balanceRepository.update, auditService.record, notificationService.create) receives the FakeUnitOfWork stubClient as its client argument.
The test suite asserts NotFoundError for an unknown request id and that the full suite (existing create/submit/approve/reject tests plus new cancel tests) passes under Jest.

constraints: Do not modify production source (src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts, leave.repository.ts, leave.routes.ts, or src/shared/types). Phase 2/3 deliverables are fixed contracts; this phase only extends tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts.

Reuse the existing eight in-memory fakes (FakeLeaveRepository, FakeBalanceRepository, FakeAuditService, FakeNotificationService, FakeValidationService, FakeEmployeeService, FakePolicyService, FakeUnitOfWork) and the containment-based transaction assertion convention already present in the suite; do not introduce a new fake or assertion style.

Tests must use the real LeaveService.cancel implementation (no mocking of the service under test) and assert observable behavior through the fakes' recorded call arrays (updateCalls, findByKeyCalls, records, inputs, callCount).

Balance-release assertions must assert the full requestedDays delta (no pro-rating) and that the balance row is read with forUpdate=true before any balance write; DRAFT cancellation must assert zero balance reads/writes.
Use future startDate fixtures (relative to Date.now()) for the success-path cancel tests so the timing guard does not reject them; use a past/today startDate only for the ConflictError timing test.
outOfScope: No production code changes: the cancel implementation, route, and AuditAction.CANCEL enum are fixed contracts from Phases 1-3 and must not be edited in this phase.
No integration/e2e tests, no route-level tests, no database or real-transaction tests — this phase is unit tests against in-memory fakes only.
No new fakes, helpers, or fixtures beyond what the existing suite already provides; no changes to the create/submit/approve/reject test blocks.

entityInvariants.invariant: A cancelled request ends in status CANCELLED with cancelledBy set to the acting actor's id and cancelledAt set to a Date; cancellation is only reachable from DRAFT (owner), SUBMITTED (owner), or APPROVED (direct manager or ADMIN), and only while startDate is strictly in the future.

Cancellation releases the full requestedDays with no pro-rating: DRAFT releases nothing, SUBMITTED decrements pendingDays by requestedDays, APPROVED decrements usedDays by requestedDays; the balance row is always read with a row lock (forUpdate=true) before any write.
Every cancellation writes exactly one audit record with action AuditAction.CANCEL, entityType 'leave_request', entityId equal to the request id, and actorId equal to the acting actor's id.

Every cancellation produces exactly one synchronous notification to the affected employee (recipientId = request.employeeId) with relatedEntityType 'leave_request' and relatedEntityId equal to the request id.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Owner may cancel own DRAFT/SUBMITTED; direct manager (employee.managerId === actor.id) may cancel APPROVED; ADMIN may cancel APPROVED for anyone (exempt from direct-manager check); no acting on own request where the manager/ADMIN rule applies. Violations throw ForbiddenError.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: ForbiddenError on authorization failure; ConflictError when startDate <= today; NotFoundError on unknown request; UnauthorizedError on missing/invalid actor.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The cancel tests must match the existing suite's containment-based transaction assertion convention: assert uow.callCount === 1 and that each participating call receives uow.stubClient, exactly as the submit/approve/reject tests do.
The cancel tests must exercise the real cancel implementation and its authorization/timing/balance-release semantics as defined in the service, without re-deriving or contradicting them.
The cancel tests must use AuditAction.CANCEL (value 'CANCEL') for the audit assertion, matching the shared enum member added in Phase 1.

The cancel tests must reuse the existing fakes and fixtures (makeRequest, makeActor, makeBalance, makeEmployee, makePolicy) and their recorded-call arrays rather than introducing parallel test doubles.

integrationPoints.why: The operation under test; its authorization, timing guard, balance release, status transition, and side effects define the assertions.
The suite to extend; its eight fakes and containment-based transaction assertions are the test harness for the new cancel cases.
The enum values the audit and status assertions must reference.
